_about: The murder line from docs/quest-schemes-plan.md §3, authored against the §6 grammar
as five linked schemes. A trader at the market asks a stranger to fetch something
from hours away; while the stranger is gone a person of standing is killed at the
lodging and the stranger is named for it. Each scheme opens on a tag the one before
it granted, so the line is five storylets that interlock, not one script. World-
agnostic: every person, place, faction and thing is a slot filled at open; no
number in any prose. §8 of the plan records what the grammar could not say and

schemes.title: A Small Favour: the errand
schemes.about: A trader's errand to the wild place, a murder at the lodging while the player is away, and guards at the market on their return.

cards.title: Fetch $errand for $giver
cards.reward: a season's custom at cost, in $giver's own words

cards.title: $giver's plan
facts: $giver is paid by $patron to see $victim dead and an outsider blamed for it.
$giver means to be at $lodging, out of sight, when it is done, and to name the stranger sent to $wild.

tell.perceptible: $witness, aside, names $victim as one $patron would sooner see gone, and wonders aloud why $giver keeps watching the door.

tell.silent: $giver shuts the stall and goes to $lodging, and keeps out of sight there.

tell.perceptible: $wild, the ground where $errand grows.
$errand, gathered, as $giver asked.

also.text: $victim was brought to $lodging and killed there while $giver kept out of sight; the stranger sent to $wild is to be named for it.

also.says: $victim is dead, found at $lodging, and the watch is asking who was seen about the place.

tell.silent: $victim is brought to $lodging and does not leave it alive.

also.text: $victim is dead at $lodging; $giver is nowhere to be seen.

tell.perceptible: $victim is dead in a room at $lodging, and the house is very quiet about it.

also.text: The guards say $victim is dead at $lodging, and that $giver named you as the stranger who was asking after them.

tell.perceptible: $captain comes up from $gate into $market with a guard at either side and asks for you by the errand you were sent on: $victim is dead at $lodging, and $giver has given your description.

also.text: $giver was found hiding at $lodging with the errand still unmade; whatever was planned there has come apart.

tell.perceptible: $giver is here at $lodging, keeping out of sight of $market, with no errand to explain it; seen, $giver makes for the door and $road.

schemes.title: A Small Favour: wanted
schemes.about: The town has your name for the killing. Two ways out at once: clear it with any two of three clues, or leave by a way the witness knows.

cards.title: Clear your name in the matter of $victim
objectives: Look at what was left on $victim, laid out at $temple
cards.reward: your name back, and $gate open to you again

cards.title: Leave by $road before the watch closes on you
objectives: Ask $witness, who knows a way past $gate
cards.reward: the open country, and a town that will not forget you

cards.title: What the town holds against you
facts: $captain has your description from $giver, and the word is out at $gate and $market.
$patron paid for this and would like it to stay as it is; $giver has gone out to $wild.

action.text: Your description is posted at $market over $captain's mark.

tell.perceptible: A notice with your description is nailed up at $market, $captain's mark under it; the stallholders have read it.

action.text: The watch at $gate has your description and turns you back.

tell.perceptible: The watch at $gate has your description, and the way out is not open to you.

tell.teller: $witness saw $giver go into $lodging that day and $victim brought in after, and will say so to $captain.

tell.perceptible: $giver's room at $lodging is empty, the house says gone out to $wild; in it, a ledger with $patron's coin set down against the day $victim died.
$victim is laid out at $temple; sewn into the coat is coin struck with $patron's mark.
Two of the three hold together: enough to know it was $giver, and $patron's coin behind $giver.
Two of the three hold together: enough to know it was $giver, and $patron's coin behind $giver.
Two of the three hold together: enough to know it was $giver, and $patron's coin behind $giver.

tell.teller: $witness knows a path onto $road that the watch at $gate does not stand on, and will show it for the asking.

tell.perceptible: $road, and the town behind you with your description on its wall.

schemes.title: A Small Favour: the one who paid
schemes.about: The giver has gone to ground at the wild place. Taken alive, the giver names the patron and owes you; killed, the name is a loose end gone and the patron is pleased.

cards.title: Find $giver, who has gone to ground
objectives: Get from $giver the name of the one who paid
cards.reward: the name, and what to do with $giver

cards.title: $giver's worth to $patron
facts: $giver alive can name $patron; $giver dead cannot, and $patron knows it.

tell.perceptible: $giver is here at $wild, with $road behind and $market behind that, and nowhere further to run.

also.text: $giver names $patron as the one who paid for it.

tell.perceptible: $giver gives up the name: it was $patron's coin, and $patron's wish.
$giver, still breathing an hour on and still in your keeping, counts that as a debt and says so.

action.text: The loose end is gone: $giver is dead.

tell.perceptible: $giver is dead. Whatever $giver knew of $patron, no court will hear it from $giver now.

schemes.title: A Small Favour: the patron
schemes.about: What the patron holds is where the proof is; what undoes it is how you win. Justice, a bargain, or too slow.

cards.title: What $patron holds, and what undoes it
objectives: Go to where $patron keeps its accounts, at $hall
Take the proof of the coin from what $patron holds there
Put it before $captain at $market, or sell it back to $envoy

cards.title: What $patron stands to lose
facts: $patron holds $hall and keeps its accounts there; what undoes $patron is the proof of what it paid for, read out in the open.
$envoy speaks for $patron and would rather buy you than fight you; $kin would rather see $captain read the proof.

also.text: $envoy has seen you at $hall and knows what you came for.

tell.perceptible: $hall is $patron's own house, and $envoy is at the door of it, expecting you.

also.text: The proof is in hand: $patron's payment for the errand, in $patron's own accounts.

tell.perceptible: In $patron's accounts at $hall: the coin paid out, and what it was paid for.
At $market, $captain reads it through twice and sends for the watch, and not for you; $kin stands by to see it done.
$envoy takes it, pays, and says $patron will remember you as a friend, for now.

tell.silent: $patron has had the days it needed; the accounts are moved from $hall and the price is set.
$patron has had the days it needed; the accounts are moved from $hall and the price is set.

schemes.title: A Small Favour: the price on your head
schemes.about: Hunters on the patron's coin, by days not hours, until the name is cleared, the region is left, or the patron is ended.

cards.title: Outlast the price $patron has set on you
objectives: Clear your name, leave the region, or end $patron
cards.reward: to sleep without a knife under the pillow

cards.title: Who $patron has sent
facts: $patron has paid hunters to find you on $road or out at $wild; they come by days, not hours, and they know $gate and $market are watched.

also.text: The first pair have found you; more will follow while $patron pays.

tell.perceptible: Two who have followed your trail from $gate down $road step out with $patron's coin in their purses.
More of them, better paid than the last; $patron has raised the price, and $wild is no safer than $road.

tell.silent: $patron withdraws the price; there is no one left to pay it.
$patron is ended, and its hunters go looking for other coin.
Far enough down $road from $market that $patron's coin does not reach.
